Status: **awaiting review — no docs written yet**

> **Update (session 2).** Four items below were resolved and implemented before the docs pass:
> Previous Versions removed, issue-link scan fixed, provider registration reworked,

Goal: replace the single 991-line `README.md` with a slim landing-page README plus a

## 1. Hard constraints confirmed by reading the source

### `scripts/release.ps1` (read in full)

| Behavior | Requirement it imposes on `README.md` |
|---|---|
| `$readmeUpdated = $readmeOriginal -replace "kat-comment-studio-<current>.vsix", "kat-comment-studio-<new>.vsix"` (line 146) | Every literal `kat-comment-studio-<version>.vsix` string in the README is rewritten. The download link and the filename mentioned in Getting Started step 3 must keep that exact literal form. It is a plain string replace — it does **not** touch link *text* like `v1.0.6`. |
| `Get-PreviousVersionEntries` (line 14) | Section heading must be exactly `## Previous Versions` at column 0. Entries must match `^\d+\.\s+\[[^\]]+\]\([^\)]+\)$` — i.e. `1. [1.0.10](https://.../dist/kat-comment-studio-1.0.10.vsix)`. Anything else in the section is dropped on next release. |
| `Set-PreviousVersionsSection` (line 52) | The section is terminated by the next `^##\s` heading. So `## Previous Versions` must be followed by another `##` heading (`## License` works) or EOF. Everything between is replaced. |
| Both functions scan `README.md` only | The Previous Versions list and the versioned download link **must stay in the root README**, not move to `docs/`. |

Consequences for the new README:
- Keep `## Previous Versions` verbatim, immediately followed by `## License`.
- Keep the two `kat-comment-studio-<version>.vsix` literals (download link + Getting Started step 3).
- **Change the download link text** from `⬇ Download v1.0.6 (.vsix)` to something version-free
  (e.g. `⬇ Download the latest release (.vsix)`), because the script never updates that text and
  it is already 5 versions stale.
- Do not introduce any other `##`-level heading between Previous Versions and License.

### Absolute URLs

Every link/image gets an absolute URL:
- pages: `https://github.com/terryaney/Extensibility.VS.Code.Comment.Studio/blob/main/docs/<page>.md`
- images: `https://github.com/terryaney/Extensibility.VS.Code.Comment.Studio/raw/main/media/<file>`

Current README uses relative `./media/...` and `media/...` (lines 3, 18, 30–35, 67, 71, 96, 112,
217, 240, 246–253, 335, 341–344, 361, 444) and in-page anchors (`#code-anchors` etc.). All must be
rewritten. Inside `docs/*.md` I'll use absolute URLs too, for consistency and because README-embedded
snippets may be copied.

## 4. Cross-page linking rules

1. Each setting is documented **once**, in `docs/settings.md`, with type/default/description.
2. Feature pages mention a setting by name and link to its row in `docs/settings.md`; they do not
   restate the default. Exception: where the default *is* the explanation (e.g. the 1000 ms
   collapse/reflow coupling), a parenthetical default is allowed.
3. Colors are documented once, in `docs/colors.md`.
4. Commands are listed once, in `docs/commands.md`; feature pages link to it.
5. Every page opens with 1–2 sentences: what it does, why you'd want it. Then a table or example.

## 5. Reported, not fixed (per "do not change runtime behavior")

- **F4 — issue-link over-matching.** `IssueLinkProvider` doesn't restrict to comment ranges, so
  `#123` in a string, a preprocessor directive, or a C# `#region` line number becomes a link.
  `anchorDecorationManager` does the right thing via `scanCommentLinesMap`. One-line-ish fix, but
  out of scope here.
- **Prefix highlighter comment detection is naive.** `findRegularCommentStart` does a plain
  `indexOf('//')` / `'#'` / `"'"` on the raw line, so a `//` or `#` or apostrophe inside a string
  literal is treated as a comment start (`var s = "don't";` → the rest of the line can be
  colorized as a `-`/`?`/etc. comment if the next char matches a prefix). `prefixHighlighter.ts:136–162`.
- **F1 — missing `dist/kat-comment-studio-1.0.11.vsix`.** Needs a release run or a commit, not a
  docs edit.
- `commentCodeLensProvider.ts:6–11` — class doc comment claims "two CodeLens items
  (Expand/Collapse + summary)"; only the summary lens is produced. Stale source comment.

## 8. Session 2 — resolved and implemented

### 8.1 Previous Versions removed (internal distribution)

- `## Previous Versions` and the `Install [previous versions](...)` line deleted from `README.md`.
- `scripts/release.ps1`: `Get-PreviousVersionEntries` and `Set-PreviousVersionsSection` deleted
  along with the entry-building block that called them. The script now only does
  version bump → `vsce package` → rewrite `kat-comment-studio-<version>.vsix` in `README.md`.
- Download link text changed from `⬇ Download v1.0.6 (.vsix)` (stale, never script-updated) to
  `⬇ Download the latest release (.vsix)`.
- **Remaining README constraint is now much smaller:** keep the two literal
  `kat-comment-studio-<version>.vsix` strings. No heading-format requirement at all.
- Older `.vsix` files remain in `dist/` — only the README list is gone.
- Superseded plan sections: §1 "Previous Versions" rows, §2 README contents, §3 F2, §7 step 6.

### 8.2 Issue-link scan fixed (F4)

`IssueLinkProvider` now walks `scanCommentLinesMap(lines)` and matches only within each line's
comment portion, converting match offsets back to absolute columns. Added guard: a match at index 0
of a comment portion that itself starts with `#` is skipped, so a PowerShell/Python comment like
`# 123 fix` → `#123` is not treated as an issue reference (the `#` is the comment marker).

Residual limitation, now shared with anchors rather than unique to issue links: `scanCommentLinesMap`
is marker-based, so `#123` inside a string on a line with no real comment can still match.
Documented in `docs/issue-links.md` rather than fixed.

### 8.3 Provider registration reworked (F7)

`SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` (a hardcoded literal duplicating `languageConfig.ts`) is gone. Replaced with
two selectors in `extension.ts`:

| Selector | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `DOC_COMMENT_LANGUAGES` | `getSupportedLanguageIds()` — derived from `languageConfig.ts` | CodeLens, comment hover, folding, reflow code actions |
| `ALL_FILES` | `{ scheme: 'file' }` | `LINK:` document links / hover / definition / completion, issue links |

Rationale: doc-comment features need a comment style from the capability table and cannot work
without one; comment-text features are pure regex and already ran everywhere via decorations.
This removes the inconsistency where a `TODO:` in a `.md` file was colorized but its `LINK:`
references and `#123` links were dead.

Safety check: `LinkCompletionProvider.provideCompletionItems` returns immediately unless
`\bLINK:\s*` precedes the cursor, so registering it on all files is not intrusive.

### 8.4 `patternProcessing.enabledLanguages` removed (F6)

The setting could only ever *subtract* from a hardcoded list, never add — an unknown language ID has
no `languageConfig.ts` entry, so nothing would render for it anyway. Its own description was wrong
(it never gated anchors). Removed from `package.json`, `types.ts`, and `configuration.ts`.

Call sites replaced with `isLanguageSupported(languageId)` from `languageConfig.ts`:
`decorationManager.ts` (×2), `autoReflow.ts` (×2), `smartPaste.ts` (×1). In `reflowCommands.ts` (×2)
the check was deleted outright — both functions already returned early on
`getLanguageCommentStyle(...) === undefined`, making it dead code.

**Settings count is now 16, not 17**, and the `patternProcessing` key table has 4 rows, not 5.
Update §3's "verified accurate" note accordingly when writing `docs/settings.md`.

### 8.7 Open decision added — markdown anchor support

You asked whether anchors should be limited to supported languages plus `*.md`. **Not implemented,
deliberately** — adding `md` to the default `fileExtensions` would produce erratic results, because
`scanCommentLinesMap` is marker-based and language-agnostic:

| Markdown line | Detected? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `<!-- TODO: fix -->` | yes | `<!--` is a block marker |
| `# TODO: fix` | yes | `#` is a single-line marker — but only because headings look like comments |
| `TODO: fix` (bare prose) | **no** | no comment marker on the line |
| `It's a NOTE: worth reading` | **yes** (false positive) | the apostrophe opens a "comment" |

That last row is the problem: apostrophes are common in prose, so markdown paragraphs would
sporadically register anchors while a plain `TODO:` at line start would not. Inconsistent enough to
be worse than no support.

**D7 — do you want real markdown support?** Options:
  a) Leave as-is. Markdown gets inline colorization only (no scan, tree, or grid). Document the gap. **(current state)**
  b) Teach `scanCommentLines` a "whole file is prose" mode for `markdown`/`plaintext`, so every line
     is scannable, and add `md` to default `fileExtensions`. Needs a language/extension argument
     threaded through `findAnchorsInText` and `AnchorDecorationManager`, plus tests. ~half a day.
  c) Add `md` to `fileExtensions` as-is and accept the erratic matching. **Not recommended.**

If you want (b), say so and I'll do it before the docs pass so the docs describe the end state.

## 9. Session 3 — lint, Markdown anchors, and the docs-site pivot

### 9.1 Lint (done)

`npm run lint` was broken — no `.eslintrc*` existed anywhere in the repo, so
`eslint src --ext ts` exited 2. Removed the `lint` script via `npm pkg delete`
and uninstalled `eslint`, `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin`, and

stays consistent (87 packages removed). Removed the `lint` row from the README
npm-scripts table. Nothing else referenced it.

### 9.2 Markdown anchor support (done)

Prior estimate was overstated. Correct framing: for prose files there is no
comment marker to find, so skip the comment map and scan every line.

`src/anchors/commentScanner.ts`
- `PROSE_LANGUAGE_IDS` = `markdown`; `PROSE_EXTENSIONS` = `.md`, `.markdown`.
- `isProseLanguageId(languageId)` / `isProseFilePath(filePath)`.
- `scanAnchorLinesMap(lines, prose)` — every line at column 0 when prose,
  otherwise delegates to `scanCommentLinesMap`.

Consumers switched to `scanAnchorLinesMap`:
- `anchorService.findAnchorsInText` — keys off `filePath` (no signature change).
- `anchorDecorationManager.updateDecorations` — keys off `document.languageId`.
- `issueLinkProvider` — same, and the leading-`#`-is-a-comment-marker guard is
  suppressed for prose so `#123` still links in Markdown.

Deliberately **not** given prose treatment:
- `prefixHighlighter` — whole-line scanning would colour every Markdown image
  (`![alt](url)`) as an alert prefix. Left marker-based.

Defaults updated in all three places: `package.json` `patternProcessing`,
`configuration.ts` fallback, `workspaceScanner.ts` `DEFAULT_SCAN_OPTIONS`.
- `fileExtensions` gains `md`.
- `ignoreFolders` gains `.vscode` — without it this repo's own
  `.vscode/Plans/*.md` (full of literal `TODO:` examples) floods the anchor
  list. Reversible via settings.

Tests: +7 in `anchorService.test.ts`, +4 in `commentScanner.test.ts`.
Suite is 350 passing (was 339). `npm run compile` clean.

### 9.3 Separate session for Markdown? No.

It was ~40 minutes of work and it changes what the docs must say (a whole
feature area gains a file type). Splitting it would have meant writing the docs
twice or coordinating across sessions. Done here, before the docs pass.

### 9.4 Docs pivot: static HTML site instead of `docs/*.md`

Supersedes §2. Modelled on `KAT.Command.Center\src\Help`: a JSON manifest, HTML
article *fragments* (semantic markup only), one stylesheet, one script that
builds the nav, routes, and generates the on-this-page TOC.

**Hosting — GitHub Pages, source `main` / `docs` folder.** Repo confirmed
PUBLIC, so Pages is free. No Actions workflow, no Jekyll, no build step: push
to `main` republishes. Enable once under Settings -> Pages.

Site URL: `https://terryaney.github.io/Extensibility.VS.Code.Comment.Studio/`

```
docs/
  .nojekyll
  index.html            shell: sidebar nav + article pane + on-this-page TOC
  assets/docs.css       adapted from help.css, VS Code dark/light palette
  assets/docs.js        manifest-driven routing, TOC, deep links
  assets/manifest.json  ordered article list (id, title, group)
  assets/images/        screenshots
  articles/*.html       one fragment per topic, semantic markup only
```

Article list is unchanged from §2 — only the format changes.

Deep links use `#/<article>/<heading-id>`, e.g.
`.../#/code-anchors/colorize`. The README links to these as ordinary external
URLs, which render correctly in the VS Code Extensions view.

Trade-offs accepted:
- No GitHub in-repo rendering of the articles (they are fragments). The README
  stays Markdown and remains the only in-repo rendered page.
- Contributors edit HTML rather than Markdown. Fragments are plain
  `h2`/`p`/`table`/`ul`, so the gap is small.
- Client-side routing means no per-page URL without JS. Acceptable for an
  internal extension.

`release.ps1` needs no change for the site to publish. If a version stamp is
wanted, add a one-line replace against `docs/assets/manifest.json`.

### 9.5 Still open

D1-D6 from §6 stand. New: confirm §9.4 before any docs are written.

### Verification performed

- `npm run compile` clean; `npm test` **350/350** across 12 files.
- `scripts/release.ps1` parses with 0 errors; the `kat-comment-studio-1.0.11.vsix`
  literal is present **3x in `README.md`** and **3x in `docs/articles/install.html`**,
  both of which the script rewrites.
- Link audit: **0** broken `#/article` or `#/article/heading` links across all
  articles and the README (every heading slug matched against the slug the JS
  actually generates).
- Asset audit: **0** unresolved references; **0** HTML classes without a CSS rule.
- Served `docs/` over HTTP: all 16 articles + assets returned 200; no JS console
  errors; no horizontal overflow; no broken images on any page.
- Behaviour verified live: hash routing, nav active state, TOC build, deep-link
  scroll, prev/next pager adjacency, nav search filter, theme toggle + persistence.

### Two issues found and fixed during verification

1. **`../media/` paths would have 404'd on GitHub Pages.** Pages serves `docs/`
   as the site root, so `..` escapes the published tree — `media/` lives outside
   `docs/` and is never deployed. All **27** references across 8 files were
   rewritten to absolute `raw/main/media/...` URLs. Verified each maps to a real
   file. (Locally these appeared to work, which is why it needed an actual
   Pages-shaped check.)
2. **TOC highlighting never activated.** `observeHeadings()` used an
   `IntersectionObserver` with `rootMargin: '-60px 0px -70% 0px'`. Jump-scrolls
   and page-top both leave zero headings inside that band, so no entry was ever
   highlighted. Replaced with a deterministic "last heading scrolled past"
   calculation on a throttled scroll/resize listener, with an explicit
   bottom-of-page case. Now exactly one entry is always active.

**Push `docs/`.** GitHub Pages is now **enabled** (source: `main`, folder
`/docs`, HTTPS enforced) at
`https://terryaney.github.io/Extensibility.VS.Code.Comment.Studio/`.

The first REST attempt returned 404 only because the `GH_TOKEN` environment
variable was overriding the repo-owner (`terryaney`) credential; clearing it and
re-issuing the call succeeded. Nothing further is needed in repo settings.

The site will not serve content until `docs/` is committed and pushed to `main`.
Until then the docs links in `README.md` will 404.

## 11. Session 5 — Follow-up fixes

Four items raised after the docs review. All resolved; **371 tests passing**
(up from 350), compile clean, 0 broken doc links.

### 11.1 Scan `.vscode` (reverted my own change)

`.vscode` was added to the scan ignore list in session 3; `.vscode-test` was
pre-existing. Removed `.vscode` from `package.json`, `configuration.ts` and
`workspaceScanner.ts`, so plan and note files under `.vscode` are scanned.
`md` stays in `fileExtensions`. Corrected the two docs pages that claimed it
was ignored (`code-anchors.html`, `settings.html`); all four sources of the
default now agree.

### 11.2 `commentCodeLensProvider` class doc

Claimed two lenses ("Expand"/"Collapse" plus summary); only the summary lens is
produced. Rewritten to describe the single lens, `codeLensMaxLength`
truncation, the deliberate SQL/PowerShell exclusion, and that `foldState` is
tracked on behalf of the fold commands.

### 11.3 EditorConfig glob matching — **fixed** (runtime change)

`parseEditorConfigFile` passed `path.basename(filePath)` and tested section
globs against that alone, while building a path-shaped regex. Any pattern
containing `/` could therefore never match.

| Section | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `[*]`, `[*.cs]` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `[*.{cs,vb}]` | ✗ silently ignored | ✓ |
| `[src/**/*.cs]` | ✗ silently ignored | ✓ |
| `[/build.cs]` | ✗ | ✓ anchored to config dir |
| `[File[0-9].cs]` | ✗ | ✓ |

Replaced the chained `.replace()` calls with `globToRegex()`, a proper
tokenizer supporting `**`, `*`, `?`, `{a,b}`, `[seq]`, `[!seq]` and backslash
escapes. `**/` matches zero directories. Unbalanced braces yield `(?!)` so the
section is skipped rather than throwing. Patterns containing `/` now match the
path relative to the `.editorconfig`; a leading `/` anchors to its directory.

New `test/unit/editorconfigService.test.ts` — 10 tests against real temp files,
covering relative-path matching, brace lists, anchoring, character classes,
`root = true` walk-stopping, closest-config-wins, and malformed sections.

**Upgrade risk — the one item worth a second look.** Sections that were
silently ignored now apply. A repo with `[*.{cs,vb}] max_line_length = 120`
will see reflow width change on upgrade. Judged correct (it is what the user
wrote and what the docs promised) but it is a real behavior change.

Note: the docs previously claimed `[*.{cs,vb}]` worked. It did not — that was a
stale-docs error introduced in session 4, now corrected.

### 11.4 `findRegularCommentStart` — **fixed** (runtime change)

The naive `indexOf` flaw was **shared**: `commentScanner.findFirstOpener` had
the same bug, so anchors, anchor decorations and issue links were affected too.
Fixed centrally rather than at one call site.

`findCommentOpener(line, from)` (exported from `commentScanner.ts`) now walks
character by character, stepping over string, template and character literals:

| Input | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `var s = "don't";` | comment at the apostrophe | code |
| `var url = "http://x";` | comment at `//` | code |
| `var s = "issue #12";` | comment at `#` | code |
| `` const s = `a // b`; `` | comment at `//` | code |
| `char c = 'a';` | comment at `'` | code |
| `Dim x = 1 ' set x` | comment | comment (unchanged) |

Backslash escapes honoured; an unterminated string consumes the rest of the
line, erring toward *not* finding a comment.

**The `'` ambiguity.** It is both a VB comment and a C-family character
literal, and the scanner has no language context. Resolved by shape: `'a'` and
`'\n'` are literals, anything else is a comment. A 3-character VB comment like
`'a'` is misread — accepted as a fair trade against the very common `"don't"`
false positive.

`prefixHighlighter.findRegularCommentStart` now delegates to it. Two behaviours
deliberately preserved: block comments and SQL `--` still get no prefix
highlighting, but scanning **continues past** them, so `x--; // ! note` still
highlights (a naive early return would have regressed this).

+11 tests in `commentScanner.test.ts`. Verified the new tests fail against the
old implementation rather than passing vacuously.

Docs updated: the prefix-highlighting "Known limitation" warning is replaced by
a note describing the new behaviour; the `scanAnchorLinesMap` doc comment no
longer cites the apostrophe misread.

## 12. Session 6 — EditorConfig scope correction

### 12.1 New finding: two EditorConfig keys are dead

While confirming the settings-vs-`.editorconfig` precedence, traced every
consumer of `getEditorConfigSettings`. All five call sites are in reflow
(`autoReflow`, `reflowCodeAction`, `reflowCommands` x2, `smartPaste`) and every
one reads **only** `maxLineLength`:

```
const maxLineWidth = editorConfigSettings.maxLineLength ?? config.reflowLineLength;
```

`customAnchorTags` and `customAnchorTagPrefixes` are parsed, stored on the
result object, and then **never read by anything**. The two
`custom_anchor_tag*` keys therefore have no effect.

The original README claimed they worked, and that claim was carried into the
new docs. It was never true.

### 12.2 Docs corrected (6 places)

| File | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `editorconfig.html` | lede, example, key table, "replace not merge" warning, resolution example all featured anchor tags | Line-width only; the two keys marked **parsed but not applied**, with a warning pointing to `patternProcessing` |
| `code-anchors.html` | "can also be configured per project with `.editorconfig`" | points to `patternProcessing`, notes the key is not applied |
| `overview.html` | "Per-project line width and anchor tags." | "Per-project reflow line width." |
| `vs-differences.html` | "support for line width and anchor tags." | "support for reflow line width." |
| `README.md` | "Per-project line width and anchor tags" | "Per-project reflow line width" |
| `editorconfigService.ts` | bare interface fields | doc comments marking both as unconsumed, so this is not re-documented as working |

**Not fixed.** Wiring anchor tags through `.editorconfig` is a feature, not a
patch — anchor scanning is workspace-wide while `.editorconfig` resolves
per-file, so it needs a design decision about how a per-file tag list applies
to a workspace-wide scan. Reported, left alone.

### 12.3 Precedence, confirmed against source

`.editorconfig` wins where it applies; the VS Code setting is the fallback
(`?? config.reflowLineLength`). Resolution is per file: walk up from the file's
directory, closest config wins, `root = true` stops the walk. Only files
matching a section header are affected. In practice only `max_line_length`
participates.

### 12.4 Release script validated in production

`scripts/release.ps1` was run by the user and produced **v1.0.12**. The
two-file loop added in session 4 worked: `README.md` and
`docs/articles/install.html` each have 3 references updated to
`kat-comment-studio-1.0.12.vsix`, zero stale `1.0.11` references, and
`dist/kat-comment-studio-1.0.12.vsix` exists. The contract holds end to end.

371 tests passing, compile clean, 0 broken doc links.
